evals.prompt: Use research-mermaid to plan a research figure from the supplied CAKE packet and original figure images. The reader should understand how the complete paradigm changes from kernel-only evolution with a fixed environment to kernel/compiler-harness co-evolution. Refer to Figure 1's visual expression. Give a concise composition decision: what appears first, how the comparison is established, which spatial/symbol/text/color choices carry the mechanism, and why this layout fits better than a plausible alternative. Do not draw, render, or edit diagram assets.
evals.expected_output: A composition for complete existing/proposed system views, grounded in Figure 1's actual visual mechanisms: coordinated panel hierarchy and common environment/task anchors, recurring role symbols, deliberate space for the added evolution mechanism and central shared harness. It does not default to two unrelated boxes, insist on equal widths or identical internal coordinates, or merge complete architectures into an A/B execution path to avoid layout work.
assertions: The decision retains identifiable complete existing and proposed system views and explains the paradigm-level change.
It uses coordinated panel hierarchy, recurring roles or symbols, and common task/environment anchors to establish comparison beyond mere proximity.
It explains deliberate extra space for the new mechanism without requiring all panel widths or internal node positions to match.
It assigns color to the evolution responsibilities, containment to composition/context, and text hierarchy to names versus explanations; it does not replace the claim with a generic dispatch example.
It rejects a merged A/B runtime path as an unsuitable shortcut for this whole-system question and makes no claim that planning proves rendered quality.

evals.prompt: Use research-mermaid to plan a figure for this synthetic rule-library process, borrowing the visual reasoning of CAKE Figure 2 from the supplied packet and image. An initial archive of error cases starts a rule library once. Each round identifies a recurring error, revises a cleaning rule, and validates the revised library against the retained archive. A new case family or a newly exposed gap starts another round of error identification; rules and archive persist. No global convergence or terminal condition is supplied. Explain the composition and the first-glance versus supporting information. Do not draw, render, or edit diagrams.
evals.expected_output: A composition transferring the separation of one-time entry, repeated work, and a return route to the correct body entry. It makes persistent rule-library/archive state and next-round triggers clear without resetting initialization, inventing a terminating diamond, or copying CAKE-specific IR names and colors as requirements.
assertions: The initial archive/library entry is spatially distinguished from the repeated identify/revise/validate body.
The return targets recurring-error identification and preserves the updated library and retained archive, rather than resetting initialization.
The trigger is a new case family or exposed gap; no invented convergence or mandatory end node is added.
Primary action labels, subordinate explanations, and return-route placement carry different jobs; the plan explains the intended reader inference.
It adapts the reference mechanism to rule-library work without prescribing CAKE's domain names or exact palette, and does not claim a rendered visual pass.

evals.prompt: Use research-mermaid to plan a figure for the supplied assay protocol in context-and-constraints.md. Borrow CAKE Figure 4's way of separating information roles, using its supplied image and source packet as a visual reference. Explain a composition that makes the specimen path primary while preserving literature/model selection, the SOP, and calibration/drift relationships. State why a plausible single serial chain or a literal copy of CAKE's two IR/compiler regions would fail. Do not draw, render, or edit diagram assets.
evals.expected_output: A transferred information hierarchy: visible specimen progression, contextual literature apart from specimen processing, SOP attached to preparation, model and coefficients attached to estimation, and drift routed to recalibration. Broad grouping does not erase required target-specific dependencies. It adapts the reference instead of imposing its IR-specific region count or flattening inputs into a chain.
assertions: Specimen preparation, acquisition, estimation, and reporting remain the primary progression.
Contextual literature is distinguished from processed inputs while its model-selection dependency and selected-model input to estimation remain explicit.
The SOP is locally associated with preparation; known-reference calibration coefficients enter estimation and unacceptable acquisition drift informs recalibration for subsequent estimates.
The composition uses grouping or supporting regions without replacing required local dependencies with a vague overall-support arrow.
It transfers information-role separation, rejects a single serial chain and literal IR/compiler-region copying, and does not equate a planning response with a rendered-quality result.
